outcome.technical:
plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py: runnable_text no longer concatenates the parts raw. A command with no shell or interpreter body comes back as split_heredocs gives its text, open quote included, so an unreadable line still reaches each guard's strict reading. When there are bodies, every part (text, each shell body, each interpreter body) goes through the new _closed_part: it walks the part with _context_step (the shared quoting reader) and appends a space when an escape is left pending, then closes every open context innermost first ('  "  )  `). A shell comment (# opening a word where commands are read, outside quotes; new helper _comment_at) is skipped, because the history guard's own lexer skips comments, and a closer added for an apostrophe inside a comment would open a quote there. That would carry into the next part and send ordinary interpreter bodies to the text reading. Pre-fix runnable view of the measured shape: "bash  
echo '
BODY
'". Post-fix: three clauses, BODY one of them. Tests: test__config.py qv1 (8 shapes: the measured shape and its twin, text ending in a double quote, a backquote or an escape, a quote crossing between shell bodies, an escape crossing between bodies, a shell body into an interpreter body), qv2 (second direction: a no-body command is returned as given and neutral parts are joined unchanged), qv3 (a comment apostrophe gains no closer; a # glued to a word is no comment). test_guard_history_rewrite.py gk34-gk37 (deny, BODY a force push; the deny comes from tr8b's shell-heredoc cd rule, so these pin the verdict), gk38-gk41 (the same four shapes with the stash verb, denied on the stash itself, which shows the operation was read), gk42 (deny: an apostrophe in an earlier body's comment opens no quote), gk43 (allow: a python body whose comment holds an apostrophe and names the stash verb is still parsed). test_guard_secrets_read.py s79/s80 (block both twins with a secret read; a lock, since that guard already blocked them through a token-anywhere arm). OUTSIDE MY FILES, edited and allowed by the plan gate: .claude/hooks/guard-uncommitted.py. Pre-fix, it read the measured stash shape as (None, operation), i.e. no refusal, so it shared the defect. Added gu54 (both twins refused on a dirty tree; red on reverted code in a scratch copy, 54/55). Replaced gu51's fixture for an untokenizable line (a shell heredoc with an odd quote, which the fix now parses as an operation; the refusal is unchanged) with a lone text line holding an odd quote. Mutations, each in a scratch copy of the tree and restored after: comment skip removed -> qv3, gk42, gk43 red; closing applied to no-body commands too -> qv2, gh25a, gh25b red; pending-escape space removed -> qv1, gk37, gk41 red; fix reverted -> gu54 red.
